newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Socialist Euro-MPs snub France again.
newsitem.headline: Socialist Euro-MPs snub France again.

text.p: Socialist Euro-MPs, cocking a snook at French President Jacques Chirac and his foreign minister, renewed on Wednesday their condemnation of France's controversial immigration bill.
In a statement clearly designed to snub Paris, the European Parliament's Socialist Group repeated its view that the French bill was "insensitive and intolerant".
It cited one leading Euro-MP saying the parliament had to remain committed to fighting "racism and xenophobia wherever it appears."

France has lashed out at the European Parliament for criticising the bill, which among other things would extend controls on non-European visitors to France, allowing fingerprinting, the impounding of passports and tighter reporting of departures.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette outraged the parliament's president on Wednesday by saying the assembly was "not worthy of the name".
Chirac launched a concerted attack on the parliament on Tuesday.
The Socialists, the largest group in the parliament, said the assembly had a right to comment on such an issue.
"We (the parliament) signed a solemn declaration in 1986...committing us to fight racism and xenophobia wherever it appears," Dutch Euro-MP Hedy d'Ancona said.
